questionText: If a = 3, find the value of (a + 12)/3.

questionText: If a = 3, find the value of a².
hints: a² means a × a. It does NOT mean a × 2!

stepByStep.text: a² means a multiplied by itself.

misconceptions.A: Calculated a × 2 = 6 instead of a × a (very common mistake!)
misconceptions.C: Calculated a + 2 = 5

questionText: If a = 3, find the value of 4a².
hints: 4a² means 4 × a². First find a², then multiply by 4.

misconceptions.C: Calculated (4a)² = 12² = 144 (squared everything, not just a)

questionText: If a = 3 and b = 5, find the value of 4ab.
hints: 4ab means 4 × a × b. Substitute the values.

misconceptions.B: Just multiplied a × b = 15, then placed digits 3 and 5 together
misconceptions.D: Added 4 + a + b = 12 instead of multiplying

questionText: If a = 3 and b = 5, find the value of 4a + b.
hints: 4a means 4 × a. Calculate that first, then add b.

misconceptions.A: Only calculated 4a, forgot to add b
misconceptions.C: Calculated 4(a + b) = 4 × 8 = 32... no. Likely 4 × 5 = 20
misconceptions.D: Calculated 4a × b = 12 × 5 = 60... no. Wrote digits a and b together

questionText: If a = 3 and b = 5, find the value of 6b − 4a.

questionText: If a = 3 and b = 5, find the value of 12 − 5a + 3b.

questionText: If a = 3 and b = 5, find the value of 4(a + b).

questionText: What is half of the square of t?
hints: Break it down: first 'the square of t' means t². Then 'half of' means divide by 2.
Square of t = t². Half of t² = t² ÷ 2.

misconceptions.A: This is half of t, not half of the square of t
misconceptions.B: This is twice the square — the opposite of half
misconceptions.D: This is the square of half of t — order matters!

questionText: The sum of d and its successor is:
hints: The successor of a number is the next number. So the successor of d is d + 1.

misconceptions.C: Added 2 instead of recognizing d + d = 2d
misconceptions.D: Multiplied d by d instead of adding

questionText: Diya has m ten-rupee notes. What is the total amount Diya has?
hints: Each note is worth ₹10, and she has m notes. Total = value × number of notes.

stepByStep.text: Each note = ₹10, number of notes = m

misconceptions.A: Forgot to multiply by 10 (treated each note as ₹1)
misconceptions.C: Added instead of multiplying

questionText: Diya has m ten-rupee notes and n five-rupee notes. What is the total amount?
questionLatex: m \text{ notes of ₹10} + n \text{ notes of ₹5} = ₹ \text{?}
hints: Calculate the value of ten-rupee notes and five-rupee notes separately, then add.
Ten-rupee notes: 10 × m = 10m. Five-rupee notes: 5 × n = 5n.

misconceptions.A: Just counted notes without multiplying by their value
misconceptions.B: Multiplied everything together instead of adding
misconceptions.D: Added all numbers individually without proper multiplication

questionText: Out of m notes of Rs. 10 each, Diya spent 12 notes to buy a cake. How many notes are left with her?
hints: She had m notes. She spent 12 notes. How many are left?
Notes left = total notes − notes spent

misconceptions.B: Reversed the subtraction (12 − m would be negative if m > 12)
misconceptions.C: Multiplied m by 10 first (the question asks for notes, not rupees)
misconceptions.D: Converted 12 notes to rupees (12 × 10 = 120) but the question asks about notes

questionText: x years ago, Soham was 8 years old. What will his age be y years hence (from now)?
questionLatex: \text{Age } x \text{ years ago} = 8. \text{ Age } y \text{ years hence} = ?
hints: x years ago he was 8. So his present age = 8 + x.
y years from now = present age + y.

stepByStep.text: x years ago he was 8, so present age = 8 + x
y years hence = present age + y
Age y years hence = 8 + x + y

misconceptions.B: Forgot to add x to get the present age first
misconceptions.C: Subtracted x instead of adding (he was 8, x years AGO, so he's older now)
misconceptions.D: Same as A — actually this is the same expression! Both are correct.

questionText: A pen costs thrice as much as a pencil. If the price of a pencil is ₹x, how much would you pay for a pen and a pencil together?

misconceptions.A: Only calculated the pen cost, forgot to add the pencil
misconceptions.C: Added 3 to x instead of multiplying x by 3

questionText: A piece of y metres was cut from a rope x metres long. What is the length of the remaining piece in metres?
questionLatex: \text{Rope} = x \text{ m}, \text{ cut} = y \text{ m}. \text{ Remaining} = ?
hints: You start with x metres and cut away y metres. What operation is that?
Cutting = subtraction. Remaining = total − cut piece.

misconceptions.B: Subtracted in wrong order (would give negative if x > y)
misconceptions.C: Added instead of subtracting

questionText: From a wire x metres long, y cm was cut. How many cm of wire is left?
questionLatex: \text{Wire} = x \text{ m}, \text{ cut} = y \text{ cm}. \text{ Left} = ? \text{ cm}
hints: The wire is in metres but the cut piece is in cm. Convert to the same unit!

stepByStep.text: Convert metres to cm: x m = 100x cm

misconceptions.A: Forgot to convert metres to cm before subtracting
misconceptions.C: Multiplied by 1000 instead of 100 (confused with mm or ml)
misconceptions.D: Multiplied x and y instead of subtracting

questionText: Which of the following pairs are unlike terms?
hints: Like terms have the SAME variable. Unlike terms have DIFFERENT variables.
Check each pair: 5a and 3a → same variable (a). 4m and 3n → different variables (m and n)!
4m and 3n are unlike terms because m ≠ n.

stepByStep.text: Like terms: same variable letter. Unlike terms: different variable letters.
